values.note: Not on recreation.gov; first come. Monongahela rules: pay the posted camping fee within half an hour of arriving at a site; at most 14 days in a 28-day period; no more than two vehicles and one wheeled camping unit per single site.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/alerts/general-use-restrictions (Forest Order: 'Occupying a campsite for longer than one-half (1/2) hour after arrival at said campsite unless the camping fee has been paid as per posted instructions', 'Camping in a developed campground for a period in excess of 14 days within a 28-day period', and the same 14-in-28 limit outside developed campgrounds; 'No more than two (2) vehicles and one (1) wheeled camping unit ... per single site') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/search?q=stonecoal (no Stonecoal facility listed) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/newsroom/releases/monongahela-increasing-and-adding-fees-several-developed (fee site, no reservation system named), read 2026-10-21

values.note: 2026 opening: April 15 ('dates are subject to change based on local weather conditions'); no closing date published.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/recreation (2026 Recreation Opening Dates, Greenbrier Ranger District: 'Stonecoal Campground FR 209 — 4/15'), read 2026-10-21

note: 15 numbered high-elevation dispersed campsites spread out along the Shavers Fork of the Cheat River. Two vault toilets and a roadside natural spring.  The dirt road is fine for most vehicles.  Reviews (2020, 4.5*) found it very quiet midweek, but every site filled on Labor Day weekend, with cars cruising the road all night.  No cell signal.  --AWH and Claude
summary: Forest Service pages: the December 5, 2025 fee release lists 'Stonecoal Campground Single Site Fee: $15' from January 1, 2026, confirming AWH's photographed fee (manual fees left untouched); the 2026 opening list gives 'Stonecoal Campground FR 209 — 4/15'. Booking confirmed not reservable / first come (not on recreation.gov) with the forest's 14-days-in-28 limit and pay-within-half-an-hour rule; season not year-round. FS road layer: FR 209 'Shavers Fork', level 3 suitable for passenger cars; no current alert or order on FR 209 (it reopened 2025-08-14 after the Red Run bridge). No Forest Service page gives a site count or numbers the sites, so the reported 15 (and whether Red Run Falls, entry 496, ~1.1 km south on FR 209, is one of them) stays unconfirmed. Note: dropped the --Claude fee sentence (fees.note carries it).
flags: Aggregator link in website: thedyrt.com. No Forest Service recreation page exists for Stonecoal (fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/recreation/stonecoal-* all 404; not in Camping & Cabins). Best agency pages: the FR 209 reopening release https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/newsroom/releases/forest-road-209-stonecoal-dispersed-camp-site-reopen-august-14 and the 2026 fee release https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/newsroom/releases/monongahela-increasing-and-adding-fees-several-developed.

Site count (for a human, re the brief): no Forest Service page gives a number of sites or numbers them. The forest's 2023 developed-dispersed list (Parsons Advocate reprint) names only 'Stonecoal Dispersed Camping (Forest Road 209)'; the 2024 Federal Register fee notice and the 2025 fee release say only 'Stonecoal campground'. The entry's 15 rests on elkinsrandolphwv.com (method reported), and no agency page says whether the Red Run Falls site (entry 496) is one of Stonecoal's sites, so the $15 fee question on 496 stays open.

Unsourced discounts: all five discount flags are stored false with no provenance; interagency_senior_access false is doubtful now that Stonecoal charges an expanded amenity fee (2024 Federal Register notice), but no page states the discount either way.
Reported (aggregator-sourced) groups left as is: hookups (thedyrt), sites count 15 (elkinsrandolphwv.com), facilities (both). No agency page confirms or contradicts them.
